nodes.summary: A finite graph $X$ *covers* a finite graph $Y$ if there is a surjective local isomorphism from $X$ to $Y$.
nodes.title: Graph cover

nodes.summary: A homomorphism from X to Y is a *simple folding* if it has one fibre consisting of two vertices at distance two, and all other fibres are singletons. A homomorphism is a *folding* if it is the composition of a non-negative number of simple foldings.
nodes.title: Folding of a graph homomorphism

nodes.summary: A finite graph $X$ is a *core* if every homomorphism from $X$ to itself is a bijection. For finite graphs $X$ and $Y$, $Y$ is a *core of* $X$ if $Y$ is a core, there is a homomorphism from $X$ to $Y$, and there is an injective homomorphism from $Y$ to $X$; that is, $Y$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of $X$.
nodes.title: Core of a graph

nodes.summary: A homomorphism $f$ from a finite graph $X$ to a finite graph $Y$ is a *local injection* if any two distinct vertices of $X$ with the same image under $f$ are at distance at least $3$ in $X$.
nodes.title: Local injection

nodes.summary: A homomorphism $f$ from a finite graph $X$ to a finite graph $Y$ is a *local isomorphism* if for every vertex $x$ of $X$, $f$ maps the set of neighbours of $x$ bijectively onto the set of neighbours of $f(x)$.
nodes.title: Local isomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $Y$ be a subgraph of a graph $X$. A *retraction* from $X$ to $Y$ is a homomorphism $f$ from $X$ to $Y$, regarded as a graph in its own right, whose restriction to the vertex set of $Y$ is the identity map. We say that $Y$ is a *retract* of $X$ if there is a retraction from $X$ to $Y$.
nodes.title: Retract

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
